subject: Urgent: Zenwell production latency & error spike after v4.1-int8 rollout
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@zenwell.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Zenwell Ops <ops@zenwell.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Production regressions after v4.1-int8 rollout - urgent

Logan,

We started seeing a sharp rise in p99 latency and 5xx error rates about 90 minutes after your team flipped to the v4.1-int8 quant profile. Our customer-facing endpoints began returning timeouts and partial outputs; downstream workers queue is spiking. Key metrics from our side: p50 ~90ms (normal), p95 ~420ms (up from ~200ms), p99 ~1.9s (previously ~520ms), and error rate jumped from 0.6% to 6.8%.

Attached is a short error summary and a trace capture (trace_profile_v4.1.zip). We consider this Sev1 for our production customers and need an immediate mitigation plan and executive visibility. Please indicate the following within the next 30 minutes:
- Root-cause hypothesis
- Immediate remediation steps you will take (rollback/traffic-shift/fallback)
- Estimated ETA to restore p99 to <700ms and error rate <1%

This is impacting revenue for three of our enterprise customers. Looping in Ops in case you need logs.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Platform, Zenwell AI

-----

Subject: Re: Production regressions after v4.1-int8 rollout - urgent

Samir — thanks for the heads up and for the attachments. I see the spike in INC-7842 in our dashboard (link below) and I’m escalating to engineering immediately.

Initial plan (short):
- We will start a controlled rollback of the v4.1-int8 profile for the affected route to the previous qprofile (v4.0-int8) within the next 20 minutes.
- Rishi will run a targeted profiler and a KV cache warm restart to clear prefix cache fragmentation.
- I’ll coordinate a traffic-shift so <50% of requests route to fallback model until p99 stabilizes.

I’ve copied Rishi and Marissa. Rishi, can you confirm rollback path and whether we need a hotfix to the decode scheduler before rollback completes? Marissa, I’ll update Zenwell once we have a clear ETA.

Link: https://app.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-7842

– Logan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir.khan@zenwell.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production regressions after v4.1-int8 rollout - urgent

Team — quick technical read from the traces Samir attached and our runtime telemetry:

Observed:
- The v4.1-int8 qprofile introduced a tighter kernel packing that reduces memory per-token but increases per-step kernel dispatch variance for sequences >512 tokens.
- Under bursty tail traffic that includes longer sequences (Zenwell has a nontrivial long-tail), we’re observing KV cache eviction thrash + decoder backpressure leading to queued microsecond-level stalls that amplify into millisecond p99 spikes.
- We also see an uptick in token-level decode failures surfaced as 5xx from the tokenizer boundary — likely due to quantization rounding edge-cases on a small subset of byte-pair combos.

Immediate remediation I recommend (ordering matters):
1) Roll back qprofile for zenwell/production route to v4.0-int8 (safe path, binary-compatible): this eliminates the scheduling variance.
2) Apply a temporary decode-scheduler cap to limit concurrent long-sequence decode concurrency (config change; no deploy).
3) Enable prefix-KV sticky routing for high-length sessions to avoid cache eviction storms.

I can kick off (1) and (2) now; rollback should start within 10 minutes and reach full traffic in ~25–35 minutes assuming no rollback collision with other flows. I’ll also open a short lived canary with 10% traffic to validate.

Supporting artifacts: profiler snapshot https://profiler.redwood.ai/session/5f7c9a2b, runtime logs excerpt in attached trace_profile_v4.1.zip.

Rishi
Sr. SRE, Serving Runtime
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Escalation: Zenwell p99/error surge — requesting exec approval for emergency rollback & credits

Irene — looping you in given revenue impact and because Zenwell has asked for exec visibility. Summary: v4.1-int8 qprofile caused tail latency and increased 5xx on high-length workloads. Rishi proposes rollback to v4.0-int8 + scheduler cap + sticky KV routing.

Requests needing leadership sign-off:
- Approve immediate rollback and any required traffic-steering (prod change) — risk is low; rollback is a config model-profile flip.
- Approve one week of service credits for zenwell’s largest impacted accounts (draft credit: 10% invoice adjustment for impacted week) to preserve relationship and expedite closure.
- If rollback completes but residual errors persist, authorize priority engineering runway for a qprofile patch (estimated 2 days).

If you approve, I’ll send a short executive note to Zenwell with times & next steps and commit to a root-cause follow-up doc tomorrow.

— Marissa
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

- Approve the proposed one-week 10% credit; Marissa, coordinate finance to prepare the credit memo.
- Rishi: if you need extra build capacity to patch qprofile, take it — treat Zenwell as priority for 48 hours.

Irene Choi

- Finance will prepare the 10% credit memo; Marissa will follow up.

Appreciate the quick coordination — we’ll send a postmortem and the long-term remediation plan.
